citations.review_text: One of the best mech games I've every played. I really feel like I'm living my best Evangelion power fantasy more than anything the Gundam games have produced. It's hard! But the challenge is worth it! I think this offers some of the best and most rewarding combat Fromsoft has produced. Will update review once I make it to Balteus

I'm loving this game. I grew up on AC 1 and 2, and while this is an entirely new game, there's enough of what I remember to hit the nostalgia bits for me. Be prepared though, as this is not an easy game that will handhold you though out. Regular enemies can be relatively easy, but each boss encounter is going to make you sweat. Take your time, learn the weaknesses, and get good at moving around, and soon you'll be feeling like a mechanical badass.
The best feeling Gundam game I have ever played. This is how a multi ton machine should feel while piloting. Non stop, action hesitation means death. When you finally get it down it's a dance.

Havent finished the game yet, but I can already recommend it. 
This review is 3 years late, so any hope for a patch to fix is long gone. It's still a good game though.
Some minor spoilers ahead.


The good

1. combat is 10/10. it's fast, flashy, responsive and you can have up to four weapons to use instead of most other games where you only have one. range matters, speed matters, timing matters, positioning matters.
2. the weapons and parts have strong variety and are thematic, despite the balancing issues. you can build a fast mech that zips around the air launching countless missiles, you can build a laser helicopter, you can build a ratatatatata tank. the customization is great.
3. weapon animations are great. specifically the missiles, they launch in a salvo and chase enemies and some will miss on fast targets. if this was any other game the devs would lazily code the missiles to all launch at once, fly like one projectile and never miss.
4. graphically it's both beautiful and gritty. although some of the office buildings look like they could use a bit more detail.
5. some boss designs are really cool thematically. giant mechs, laser beam spiders, spaceships.


The bad

1. the heavy reuse of maps. although i wouldnt call this a negative per se but it could be so much better.

Title: Mechs, Missiles, and FromSoftware at Its Best: 8/10

Armored Core VI: Fires of Rubicon was my first dive into the Armored Core franchise, and as a longtime fan of FromSoftware's Souls games, I wasn't sure what to expect. What I found was a fast paced, highly customizable mech game that rewards experimentation and skill just as much as any Souls title.

The customization is easily the star of the show. Every mission gave me an excuse to tweak my AC, swap out weapons, adjust my frame, and find the build that fit both my playstyle and the challenge ahead. It never felt like there was a single "correct" answer just the satisfaction of engineering your own solution.

Combat is frantic in the best way possible. Boosting through missile barrages, staggering enemy ACs, and unloading an arsenal of high powered weaponry never really gets old. The boss fights, in particular, are classic FromSoftware: demanding, rewarding, and incredibly satisfying once you finally overcome them.

The mission based structure is also a refreshing change of pace. Instead of a massive open world, Fires of Rubicon keeps things focused, allowing missions to stay varied while encouraging replayability to unlock different endings and make new decisions.

The story is surprisingly engaging, even if it's delivered in FromSoftware's signature "piece it together yourself" style. The cast of handlers, mercenaries, and rival pilots all leave an impression despite rarely meeting them face to face.

My biggest criticism is that some missions can begin to feel repetitive, and unless you're constantly experimenting with new builds, combat can settle into a comfortable routine. The learning curve can also be intimidating for newcomers, especially early on.

Overall: 8/10

While the story is amazing and the idea is fun the gameplay falls flat. Most of the guns either hit like wet pool noodles or don't track at all. The enemies are so poorly balanced as well. A majority of the game you'll easily body then there's the one boss that forces you to completely change ac's just to stand a chance. 

Let's take a boss called the enforcer as an example. He starts off with a lazar that if you don't have a fast mech it WILL hit you at the start. Then he has a bubble gun that is damn near impossible to avoid so that's melting your health. Then if you're on the floor he can do a melee attack that has huge reach and will damn near one shot you. All while you only have 3 heals and he has a huge healthpool. 

Or this one boss called the Smart Cleaner. It's just an absurdly tanky boss, has an insta kill attack, really poor hitboxes that will drag you in front of him from far away, and aoe attacks that come out of nowhere. I won against him 2 different times and both times I completely ran out of ammo. He is so tanky that I would have to melee him at the end just to finish him off. 

Then there's the keybinds. For some reason I cannot use core expansions. I've looked at it and it says assault boost + shift. Doesn't do it. I can guarantee I had it equipped when I was trying to do it. I physically couldn't use the thing I bought. 

Finally there's the weapons. They range from slap them with a pool noddle, or fails to even hit them. The only reliable weapon I've found is double shotguns, miniguns, or melee. Almost everything else falls into the other category. 

I genuinely want to like this game. I love fromsoft and their games but this one just feels so bad.

Armored core 6 is my favorite game of all time with the only thing even coming near it being ultrakill. Everything from its story, characters, gameplay, and music is amazing.

I bought armored core 6 originally on Playstation when it came out and just recently bought it on pc during the summer sale which is why my hours are so low on steam.

No game that i have ever played has been able to match how much I enjoyed this game and I dont think anything will until they make another entry in the franchise (or if they make another spiderman game better than spiderman ps4 but that's a pipe dream).

Please for the love of god fromsoft make a new one im begging you this game ignited my love for robots I just want another entry please.

claims.claim: The game runs well on the technical side, though one reviewer notes performance issues stemming from the anti-cheat system which can be mitigated by playing offline.

citations.review_text:
Explanation to most "concerns" from "die hard" fans in a bit but generally this game is probably the most fun i've had in a while, it has a decently steep learning curve like every fromsoft game but once you learn what the stats do and how to make your ac YOUR AC based off your playstyles then the game becomes amazing.

Yes there are "cheese" methods KINDA but most of it is pray and hope, the way I see it, play how you feel like a mech should play in your eyes. A speedy light flying smg running and constant dopamine build, a literal tank that not only has canons but also miniguns or whatever you really want, hell play the whole game by only punching with your metallic fists.

At the end of the day the game is played how you make it but it never misses making you feel cool and that is the whole point of it, you are meant to be lower then everyone that did everything "right" but you exist in your own league so act like it.

The game also features 3 separate endings which are unlocked after atleast ONE whole playthrough (the game in itself isn't actually "long") and each ng+ or ng++ playthrough brings different decisions with different rewards, different secrets and 90% of them are story changing.

Now to the thing I mentioned at the very start, the main complain you will probably see is 

"Game running bad" - this is due to the anti cheat there aren't many work arounds except playing exclusively offline and disabling it.

"This game does not compare to the older ones" or anything in the area of this complaint - This is redundant as how fromsoft went through with this series from the very start is that it is split in "Generations" which certain games are part of and each Generation is meant to be somewhat or entirely different from the others. This argument is redundant as you are not meant to compare this game to the others but instead look at it as its own thing for that is what it is, Armored Core 6 is currently the only game in the "6th Gen" and cannot compare to 5…

++

Bought it in the recent sale and am very happy. Completed all endings and now grinding for all parts, logs, and S rank. Wish they had a quick restart button for replaying missions though. Same for ranked matches. 

Ran surprisingly well, but it was hotter than I would have liked so I swapped to the minimum graphic settings and other than small issues with shadows, ran even better considering I have integrated GPU.
Runs great and it is easily one of the best combat systems ever.

I thought of comparing it to Doom but made for controllers, but after playing it some more, it stands on its own feet. You can play as a tank, something balanced or as a fighter jet. All playstyles are valid. Very well optimized. Controls feel like you are piloting a massive, overly maneuverable mech. Maybe some bosses feel over-tuned, so do not feel ashamed to look up a tutorial, but I guess it provides a challenge for those looking for it outside the arena. 9.99/10

"This game does not compare to the older ones" or anything in the area of this complaint - This is redundant as how fromsoft went through with this series from the very start is that it is split in "Generations" which certain games are part of and each Generation is meant to be somewhat or entirely different from the others. Super replayable due to the large Mech options and NG+ variations on missions. Super smooth and flowing combat that is challenging but fair

If you like FromSofware's other games, you'll like this. If you don't like FromSoftware's other games, you'll probably like this anyway since it's nothing like their souls games. There's a bit of a learning curve, but it's not too difficult once you get the hang of making a decent loadout. Singleplayer and PvP are both great. The story is on the shorter side, but NG+ has extra content.

I just finished Armored Core 6 in its entirety and here are my honest thoughts.

Right out of the box, its an AMAZING GAME. The story is immersive, the action is intense, and there are great customization options available. The progression is very linear and straightforward, with lots of secrets and decisions to make. The soundtrack is also great! It adds to the immersion to the entire game, and I really recommend getting into it.

This is a personal preference but don't let it stop you from playing this game. There are three endings, but I prefer one of the two other endings than the true ending, because this game is not sunshine and rainbows for all the characters involved. It's dark, its gritty, and while I am expecting this on an Armored Core game, I just felt that the final "true" ending was a bit anticlimactic and overall a worse decision than the other two. I mean, there is a clear "better" ending.

Anyway, I think the story is, in it of itself, an amazing, self-contained premise. You really should experience it for yourself.

I give this game an 8/10!

Explanation to most "concerns" from "die hard" fans in a bit but generally this game is probably the most fun i've had in a while, it has a decently steep learning curve like every fromsoft game but once you learn what the stats do and how to make your ac YOUR AC based off your playstyles then the game becomes amazing.

Yes there are "cheese" methods KINDA but most of it is pray and hope, the way I see it, play how you feel like a mech should play in your eyes. A speedy light flying smg running and constant dopamine build, a literal tank that not only has canons but also miniguns or whatever you really want, hell play the whole game by only punching with your metallic fists.

At the end of the day the game is played how you make it but it never misses making you feel cool and that is the whole point of it, you are meant to be lower then everyone that did everything "right" but you exist in your own league so act like it.

The game also features 3 separate endings which are unlocked after atleast ONE whole playthrough (the game in itself isn't actually "long") and each ng+ or ng++ playthrough brings different decisions with different rewards, different secrets and 90% of them are story changing.

Now to the thing I mentioned at the very start, the main complain you will probably see is 

"Game running bad" - this is due to the anti cheat there aren't many work arounds except playing exclusively offline and disabling it.

"This game does not compare to the older ones" or anything in the area of this complaint - This is redundant as how fromsoft went through with this series from the very start is that it is split in "Generations" which certain games are part of and each Generation is meant to be somewhat or entirely different from the others. This argument is redundant as you are not meant to compare this game to the others but instead look at it as its own thing for that is what it is, Armored Core 6 is currently the only game in the "6th Gen" and cannot compare to 5…

If you like FromSofware's other games, you'll like this. If you don't like FromSoftware's other games, you'll probably like this anyway since it's nothing like their souls games. There's a bit of a learning curve, but it's not too difficult once you get the hang of making a decent loadout. Singleplayer and PvP are both great. The story is on the shorter side, but NG+ has extra content.

OK I'm a FromSoftware fan based on how much I like their games, but I did not expect to like AC6 this much.

I dropped it after 2 levels because it felt boring, then I read a few info online about "changing builds being core gameplay and part of the fun", and that's what got me: I started playing with builds and the game turned a lot more fun.

I discovered melee was a thing and focused on that build, but then later on I discovered I love big booms and also fast moving mechas.

Overall, while the game could look fast paced, I never perceive it like that: like most FromSoftware games, it feels like driving a tank, you can determine if you are going to be hit an entire second before the attack  hits you.
There is time to think between each attack and deciding your next move is important in avoiding damage.

Making your cool mecha is amazing, this is possibly the first mecha game I actually enjoyed. The story is fun, and just heads up you gotta finish the game multiple times to see it all.

Highly recommended, it felt like a souls game with fighting only, essentially.

Fun and challenging game.
Robot graphics are great, but not the environment, trees are very cheap graphics.
Wanted to rage quit from beginning, but decided to let it play out, and in the end started to enjoy it.
If you're stuck on some hard enemy, just rethink your bot configuration/design, try out different builds/weapons.

claims.claim: Players can swap out their mech's entire body, armor, and weapon loadouts between attempts at difficult encounters or missions.

citations.review_text:
[h2]It’s an open book exam but all the answers must come from within.[/h2]
FromSoftware back at it again, delivering a deceivingly strategic game enshrouded in speed and fire power. 



[b]Miyazaki’s Way[/b]

The Guardian published an interview of Hidetaka Miyazaki where he famously said that he [i]sucked[/i] at video games and that he uses everything at his disposal. This was his approach for Elden Ring and its debated expansion. Armored Core 6 was already a year old at the time of the interview. After having experienced the rebirth of this beloved title, I swear that he is talking about Armored Core 6 rather than Elden Ring.

Typical to any FromSoft game, I died a lot. After every failed attempt, Miyazaki would reveal his presence in the options. He would stare me right at the face in the form of a menu choice. The game would gently give me the option to change my build.

“Big deal!” some would say. It can be argued that in all souls like games, you could almost always change your build before entering a boss fight. Though that is true, the range of modification has never been as open as Armored Core 6. Yes, you can change your armor, rethink your weapons before attempting at Malenia once again. Armored Core bested this option by not only allowing you to change your weapons load out, but it also allows you to change your Core’s entire body. Speed legs on your first 5 attempts, then full on tank build once frustration sets in. Imagine Elden Ring allowing you to fully redistribute your stats prior to every attempt because that is how liberating this game is. In every crucial step of the game, it offers everything at your disposal.


[b]Facilitation Anticipation[/b]

Lets move on to my favorite design aspect of the game.

Souls like games have always accommodated the majority of builds that players may throw at its bosses: “Mage build you’ve got there? [i]Go on, you can do it! [/i]Poison dagger build? [i]Get in there, you’ll be fine...[/i] Double great sword with a l…

Possibly one of the best action game I have ever played.

First, before even getting into combat there are a lot of customization for the mech (an "armored core" or "AC"), which can drastically alter it's behavior and stats, allowing the player to choose their own playstyle (whether it's actually viable or not is a different matter). For PVE, most build will be able to clear the campagin, depending on skill level. Furthermore, there is often no clear "upgrade", as in this components are strictly better than its counter part, all of them get trade off. For example, a bigger gun will have more damage but also significantly heavier, affecting other functions of the AC.

The game is set up as a series of short missions, which can vary in length, at like 10 or 15 minutes max. For me, this is quite addictive as I more often than not keep saying "just one more mission" and then end up playing for more than an hour. This also makes testing build very convenient, and the game allows for changing build mid-mission at checkpoints if you fails.

The mechanic during combat is also simple, not very complex control. An AC feel fast and powerful, it feels very different from just another third person shooter but with a mech skin, it does feel like controlling a machine. The combat is typically very fast, but a rythym is still required with reload, heat managements for weapons (there can be four firing simultaneously at the same time), coupled with energy management for the AC, which control dash, fly,.... Therefore, it doesn't feel like mindless button mashing (which can technically still work with certain builds and levels) and does take some skills to do well, which is very sastifying.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that completing the campaign multiple times across New Game plus playthroughs unlocks new missions, alternate storylines, and different mission opportunities.

citations.review_text:
One of, if not the best mecha games out there. The story is all in all amazing and the pvp isn't too bad either, you can well enjoy the game as just a single-player game. 
One of my personal favorite games ever, includes the best boy V.IV Rusty.
I know replaying games isn't for everyone, i can highly giving this one a few playthroughs. The ng+ doesn't add stats to enemies but instead offers variation to missions and additional story. If you have the patience, please play it three times to get the full experience.

(edit) After knowing the game and how to run through missions on ng+ and beyond the whole start to end of ng+2 took around 30 hours

I literally cannot think of another Mech game that even comes close to this. This is the dream of every MechWarrior 2 kid... the embodiment of everything we've ever wanted. 

You're a massive metal husk with guns and thrusters... and chaos ensues. 

I won't say any more than that. You need this game in your life. 

Note: You need to play the Campaign 3 times in order to unlock the true ending. Each run through is different. Same missions, but different opportunities happen.

An absolute gem of a game that I wish more people played.  Seriously, this game has one of the best presented stories in a game that I've ever seen coupled with fast and arcade-like gameplay.  The amount of customization you have with your armored core is seriously impressive and makes it really feel like your own.  I simply cannot get enough of this game and there's too much for me to explain every single thing that I adore about this game.  With the way it handles NG+ and NG++, and all the alternate missions, storylines, collectables, arena fights, and interactions that all made me appreciate the amount of effort and care put to every single detail is unmatched.  It is such a shame that not enough people don't give this game a try because it is truly amazing, please do yourself a favor and play this game.

TL;DR One of, if not the greatest action adventure RPGs to date.

Full Review:

I'll be completely honest, I am a hardcore AC fan. My dad played. I played. I have some of my fondest memories with this franchise, and this game is just an upgrade in everyway... unless you've played For Answer :*)

As far as AC:VI Fires of Rubicon, I had a blast and still am after playing the story 3 times (different endings each time with new missions) im not a completionist by any means but this one was fun to do!

If you never tried Armored Core, you can get through a lot before the 2 hour window and see how you like it and refund it if you don't.

claims.claim: Reviewers point out that the game lacks a field of view (FOV) slider.

citations.review_text:
Armored Core 6 is the very first armored core game I have ever played, and instantly became my favorite game of all time despite grappling with the mechanics.

Fills the power fantasy while also providing a challenge. Only complaint is a lack of an FOV slider which would be very helpful for some bosses. 

My friends find the game rather difficult, mostly because there is no difficulty slider- yet you can build your mech to become more or less twitchy or unstoppable to compensate.

Runs decently well on a mid-level computer.

AC6 is a fantastic action game that has some of the best art direction and spectacle bosses Fromsoft has ever produced. It also has an incredible electronic soundtrack that I'd buy the deluxe edition for all on its own. 

The gameplay is tight, responsive, and generally very fun as you come up with solutions to blast through missions. That said it does suffer from compounding balance issues that sour the experience a bit. These mostly revolve around the stagger mechanic, energy management, and the awkwardness of how 3-dimensional dodging lacks a way to descend quickly. 

I still recommend the game though despite the flaws. The first-playthrough experience is very enjoyable as the story unfolds and crafting your own mech is just too damn cool.

citations.review_text:
I thought this was just a game, but I'm a mech pilot in real life now.

The gameplay is incredibly, alarmingly dialed-in to perfection. There are no difficulty options, so rest assured you're playing the exact game the developers intended. Also the soundtrack is obnoxiously good.

The single player campaign is perfect, and thank goodeness because multiplayer is a bit jank: inexplicably FromSoftware has still not figured out how to write decent netcode. PVP is not good over a 300 ping connection, and the idiot matchmaker can and will match you against a guy who's on the opposite side of the planet.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as lacking a traditional leveling system, tying difficulty and progression instead to mech assembly and parts selection.

citations.review_text:
Armored Core VI won me over in an insanely short period of time compared to other games I play. I have dreams about piloting an AC The way this game makes me feel like a god in a 3-story tall metal carapace is a feeling I can only wish I could have in my own lifetime. At time of review I have completed every achievement at 115 hours, and I can see myself playing this game for countless hundreds more. The way the story is written is captivating. Fromsoft really pulled out the PCA Satellite for this one.  Rusty is my favorite character by a long shot and I know I'm not alone in that. Every cutscene was cool asf too, I found myself spamming my screencap button on multiple occasions.

As far as gameplay, this is classic fromsoft. A lot of the difficulty comes from how well you build your AC, seeing as how there's not really any leveling system, but even if your builds are sub-optimal, you'll probably still be able to play through the entirety of the campaign with a little difficulty. AC6 gives you a little bit of help by providing straightforward descriptions of what each stat does, as well as prebuilt ACs that you get from progressing in the game, but it's still up to you to put together a strong AC. In classic Fromsoft style, the skill ceiling of actually piloting your AC is crazy high, but learning to pilot your AC effectively is a very, very enjoyable process. 

If you can buy this game, buy it. It's worth it,

Boring stuff: My rig is really nothing special and I don't think this game has lagged for me once. I've got a decent graphics card that ran me about 300$ and I believe it's still close to that at time of writing. I have 32 gb of DDR4, which *was* affordable when I purchased it but our AI generated overlords have decreed that nothing is safe. I'm not a computer nerd but I've attached my specs for those interested. Game is smooth as butter.

Been a fan of the series for a while, so I can't say I'm entirely unbiased, but I'll keep gushing to a minimum. Here are the facts:
   1. From Software made Dark Souls, so you know that gameplay will be balanced... until it is not. Bosses can be very OP, and it can be frustrating when you have to rely on a build or tactic that is outside your comfort zone, but you must adapt and overcome. The truth is that there is a way to beat every boss. As your skill improves, you may even find yourself creating new way of winning! Keep in mind that every part is viable. Even the starting blade has merit because it does more damage to energy shields than any melee weapon in the game.
   2. There is a lot of depth to this game. Lore in your face, hidden lore in part descriptions, implied lore in combat logs, and lore that changes between timelines; you have to beat the game three times just to have access to every story mission: Insane! The story is so impressive, there is no way it could be condensed into a single movie. (God, I hope they don't make a movie! Maybe an anime... maybe...)
   3. Your creativity will flourish. The decal system alone is so meticulous that it is almost a visual arts tool in its own right! You could create the same build a thousand different ways and still never scratch the surface of what you could do! They even give you a photo tool in the in-mission pause menu!
   4. From Software cares more about this franchise than Souls. Every Armored Core is a passion-project for them, so I promise you this game is good! Mecha may not be as popular in America as Japan, but with a game this good, that might change! Armored Core is here to stay! (I warned you I was biased!)
     Let's review. Pros: smooth balanced gameplay, incredible story, fostering of critical thinking and creativity, made by a team who cares about the game! Cons: Hard bosses, sort of, but not really. Just get good, lol kidding: you WILL get good!

The gameplay is incredibly, alarmingly dialed-in to perfection. There are no difficulty options, so rest assured you're playing the exact game the developers intended. Also the soundtrack is obnoxiously good.

The single player campaign is perfect, and thank goodeness because multiplayer is a bit jank: inexplicably FromSoftware has still not figured out how to write decent netcode. PVP is not good over a 300 ping connection, and the idiot matchmaker can and will match you against a guy who's on the opposite side of the planet.

Fantastic Mecha game with lots of replayability and an excellent campaign.  Only downside is the campaign gets old after running through it 8 times, and there aren't really other game modes.  The PvP is available but both limited and the hosting and backend structure are a bit primitive.  In short it's not supported very well and I don't consider it part of the game.

Nevertheless, the single player experience is, as I said, fantastic.  Here I go for campaign run number 9 ...

[h1]Undoubtedly, this is one of the [b][u]BEST MECH[/u][/b] games available on Steam to date.[/h1]
I bought the Deluxe Edition at full price, and it was worth every penny spent.

This is my first exposure to the [i][b]Armored Core[/b][/i] series. I have no prior experience with the older games of the series. But it instantly becomes one of my favorite video games of all time. The combat is fast, smooth, and fluid.

The mech customization is very extensive, from ranges of available weapons (melee, guns, and two shoulder-mounted slots) down to the custom decals editor. (You can even paint your whole mech with gradients if you know the way.)

Your mechs can be built into roughly three categories: light, medium, and heavy. Personally, I prefer hit-and-run glass cannon mechs because of their insane moving speed and their fast and frequent dodging. It was fun! But there are no cookie cutters. Some missions require a specific build, which will help you go through it a lot easier.

The graphics are very detailed, especially those eye-candy particle effects, and the sound design is strong, stunning, and epic. The story is deep and profound. Voice acting is very cool.

[h2]Overall, [b]9/10.[/b] Soulslike fans must play this masterpiece at least once in life![/h2] A point was deducted because of the multiplayer mode. My internet connection is a bit unstable. I saw my opponent warping from place to place. And before I knew it, they already staggered me and... BOOM.
Anyways, if you don't mind the multiplayer mode, it is still one of the best single-player games out there.
